chapters.title: Chapter1 - Analogy : Basic & Relationship
chapters.content:
PART 1 — ANALOGY KA BASIC CONCEPT
Sabse pehle ek line yaad rakho:
Analogy = Do cheezon ke beech jo relationship hai, wahi relationship doosri do cheezon ke beech find karna.
Iska common format:
A : B :: C : ?
Isko padhte hain:
A is related to B in the same way C is related to ?
Example 1
Dog : Puppy :: Cat : ?
Socho:
Dog ka baby → Puppy
Toh Cat ka baby → Kitten
Answer = Kitten
Yahan relationship hai:
Animal → Baby
________________________________________
Example 2
Hand : Finger :: Foot : ?
Hand mein kya hota hai?
→ Finger
Foot mein kya hota hai?
→ Toe
Answer = Toe
Relationship:
Whole → Part
________________________________________
Example 3
Bird : Fly :: Fish : ?
Bird ka characteristic/action?
→ Fly
Fish ka characteristic/action?
→ Swim
Relationship:
Animal → Action
________________________________________
🔑 Sabse important point
Analogy mein answer ko directly guess nahi karna hai.
Pehle:
Step 1
A aur B ka exact relationship identify karo.
Step 2
Usi relationship ko C par apply karo.
Step 3
Answer nikalo.
Example:
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
Pehle:
Doctor → Hospital
Relationship:
Person → Workplace
Ab:
Teacher → ?
School
✅ Answer = School
________________________________________
Analogy mein relationships ke bahut saare types hote hain
Abhi sirf inko identify karna seekho:
1. Person → Workplace
Doctor : Hospital
Teacher : School
2. Animal → Baby
Dog : Puppy
Cat : Kitten
3. Whole → Part
Body : Hand
Hand : Finger
4. Object → Function
Pen : Write
Knife : Cut
5. Person → Tool
Carpenter : Hammer
Farmer : Plough
6. Place → Thing found there
Library : Books
Museum : Artifacts
7. Cause → Effect
Fire : Smoke
Rain : Flood
8. Synonym
Big : Large
Small : Little
9. Antonym
Hot : Cold
Day : Night
10. Young → Adult
Calf : Cow
Foal : Horse
CET ke liye in relationships ko identify karna bahut important hai.
________________________________________
🧠 Ek golden trick
Question dekho:
A : B :: C : ?
Apne mind mein ye sentence banao:
"A ka B se kya relation hai?"
Phir:
"C ka same relation kis se hai?"
Bas.
📝 Ab Part 1 ki mini practice
Q1. Book : Read :: Food : ?
A) Cook
B) Eat
C) Buy
D) Serve
Q2. Eye : See :: Ear : ?
A) Speak
B) Hear
C) Walk
D) Touch
Q3. Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
A) Court
B) School
C) Bank
D) Market
Q4. Puppy : Dog :: Kitten : ?
A) Cow
B) Cat
C) Horse
D) Goat
Q5. Finger : Hand :: Toe : ?
A) Leg
B) Foot
C) Arm
D) Head
PART 1 — LEVEL 2: Relationship Identification
Analogy mein sabse badi mistake hoti hai:
A aur B ke beech koi bhi relation dekhkar answer laga dena.
Humein exact relation pakadna hai.
Example:
Pen : Write :: Knife : ?
Pen ka kaam → Write
Knife ka kaam → Cut
✅ Answer = Cut
Yahan relation hai:
Object → Function
________________________________________
🔹 Type 1: Object → Function
Question	Relation	Answer
Pen : Write	Object → Function	Write
Knife : Cut	Object → Function	Cut
Camera : Photograph	Object → Function	Photograph
Thermometer : Temperature	Object → Function	Measure temperature
पहचानने की trick:
Khud se pucho:
"Pehli cheez ka kaam kya hai?"
________________________________________
🔹 Type 2: Person → Workplace
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
Doctor kaha kaam karta hai?
→ Hospital
Teacher kaha kaam karta hai?
→ School
✅ School
Examples:
•	Judge : Court 
•	Farmer : Farm 
•	Pilot : Airport 
•	Chef : Kitchen 
Trick:
"Ye person normally kaha kaam karta hai?"
________________________________________
🔹 Type 3: Whole → Part
Hand : Finger :: Foot : ?
Hand ka ek part → Finger
Foot ka ek part → Toe
✅ Toe
Examples:
•	Car : Wheel 
•	Tree : Branch 
•	House : Room 
•	Book : Page 
Trick:
"B pehli cheez ka ek hissa hai?"
________________________________________
🔹 Type 4: Animal → Young One
Dog : Puppy :: Cat : ?
Dog ka young one → Puppy
Cat ka young one → Kitten
✅ Kitten
Examples:
•	Cow : Calf 
•	Horse : Foal 
•	Lion : Cub 
•	Goat : Kid 
________________________________________
🔹 Type 5: Animal → Sound
Dog : Bark :: Cat : ?
Dog ki sound → Bark
Cat ki sound → Meow
✅ Meow
Examples:
•	Lion : Roar 
•	Snake : Hiss 
•	Horse : Neigh 
•	Cow : Moo 
________________________________________
🔹 Type 6: Synonym
Big : Large :: Small : ?
Big = Large
Small = Little
✅ Little
Yahan dono words ka same/similar meaning hai.
Examples:
•	Happy : Glad 
•	Fast : Quick 
•	Begin : Start 
•	Smart : Intelligent 
________________________________________
🔹 Type 7: Antonym
Hot : Cold :: Day : ?
Hot ↔ Cold
Day ↔ Night
✅ Night
Examples:
•	Up : Down 
•	Rich : Poor 
•	Black : White 
•	Old : Young 
________________________________________
🔥 सबसे जरूरी बात
Exam mein kabhi-kabhi ek pair ke beech multiple relations possible hote hain.
Example:
Bird : Nest
Bird nest mein rehta hai.
To relationship:
Animal → Home
Ab:
Lion : ?
→ Den
Isliye answer Tiger nahi hoga, kyunki humein same relationship chahiye.
________________________________________
🧠 5-Second Method
Har analogy mein ye 3 steps follow karo:
Step 1
A → B ko dekho
Step 2
Pucho:
"A ka B se exact relation kya hai?"
Step 3
Same relation:
C → ?
________________________________________
Example
Book : Page :: Tree : ?
Book ka part → Page
Tree ka part → Branch
✅ Branch
________________________________________
🎯 Ab tumhara next test
Ab main 10 questions dunga, lekin is baar options ke saath. Isse pata chalega ki relationship genuinely samajh aa gaya ya sirf examples yaad hue hain.
Q1. Bird : Nest :: Lion : ?
A) Forest
B) Den
C) Cage
D) Tree

B) Cut
C) Steel
D) Sharp

Q10. Car : Wheel :: Human : ?

🧠 PART 2A — Word Analogy: Relationship ko पकड़ना
Basic format:
A : B :: C : ?
Humein A → B ka relationship identify karke wahi C → ? par lagana hai.
________________________________________
1️⃣ Profession → Place
Example:
Teacher : School :: Doctor : ?
Teacher ka workplace = School
Doctor ka workplace = Hospital
✅ Answer: Hospital
Aur examples:
•	Lawyer → Court 
•	Farmer → Farm 
•	Chef → Kitchen 
•	Pilot → Airport 
•	Soldier → Army 
⚠️ Dhyan do: kabhi-kabhi profession aur workplace confusing ho sakte hain.
Teacher : School
Yahan relationship person → workplace hai, na ki person → profession.
________________________________________
2️⃣ Profession → Tool
Ye bahut important pattern hai.
Carpenter : Saw :: Barber : ?
Carpenter ka tool = Saw
Barber ka tool = Scissors
✅ Answer: Scissors
Examples:
•	Doctor → Stethoscope 
•	Farmer → Plough 
•	Tailor → Needle 
•	Painter → Brush 
•	Writer → Pen 
Trick:
Pucho:
"Ye person apna kaam karne ke liye kya use karta hai?"
________________________________________
3️⃣ Object → Function
Pen : Writing :: Knife : ?
Pen ka function = Writing
Knife ka function = Cutting
Examples:
•	Camera → Photography 
•	Refrigerator → Cooling 
•	Clock → Time 
•	Thermometer → Temperature 
•	Keyboard → Typing 
Trick:
"Is object ka main purpose kya hai?"
________________________________________
4️⃣ Material → Product
Ye bhi frequently useful pattern hai.
Gold : Jewellery :: Wood : ?
Gold se jewellery banti hai.
Wood se kya banta hai?
→ Furniture
✅ Answer: Furniture
Examples:
•	Leather → Shoes 
•	Cotton → Cloth 
•	Wheat → Flour 
•	Milk → Butter 
•	Clay → Pot 
Trick:
"Pehli cheez se doosri cheez banti hai?"
________________________________________
5️⃣ Animal → Home
Lion : Den :: Bird : ?
Lion ka home = Den
Bird ka home = Nest
Examples:
•	Dog → Kennel 
•	Horse → Stable 
•	Cow → Shed 
•	Rabbit → Burrow 
•	Bee → Hive 
________________________________________
6️⃣ Cause → Effect
Fire : Smoke :: Rain : ?
Fire se kya hota hai?
→ Smoke
Rain ka possible effect?
→ Flood
Relationship:
Cause → Effect
⚠️ Yahan exact relationship dekhna important hai.
________________________________________
7️⃣ Object → Material
Chair : Wood :: Ring : ?
Chair kis material se commonly bani hoti hai?
→ Wood
Ring?
→ Gold
Examples:
•	Shirt → Cotton 
•	Bottle → Glass 
•	Table → Wood 
•	Coin → Metal 
________________________________________
🔥 Ab ek important CET technique
Kabhi question mein options mein related words ke multiple answers honge.
Example:
Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
Options:
A. Book
B. School
C. Student
D. Pen
Teacher ka Book se bhi relation hai, Student se bhi relation hai.
Lekin Doctor → Hospital ka exact relation hai:
Profession → Workplace
Isliye:
Teacher → School
✅ B
याद रखो:
सबसे common relation नहीं, बल्कि सबसे EXACT relation चुनना है।
________________________________________
📝 PART 2A Practice
Abhi difficult questions nahi. Pehle relationship identification strong karte hain.
Q1.
Carpenter : Saw :: Barber : ?
A) Chair
B) Scissors
C) Hair
D) Shop
Q2.
Gold : Jewellery :: Wood : ?
A) Tree
B) Furniture
C) Forest
D) Paper

Dog : Kennel :: Horse : ?
A) Stable
B) Farm
C) Cage
D) Field
Q4.
Cotton : Cloth :: Leather : ?
A) Animal
B) Shoes
C) Thread
D) Bag
Q5.
Fire : Smoke :: Rain : ?
A) Water
B) Cloud
C) Flood
D) River
Q6.
Doctor : Stethoscope :: Farmer : ?
A) Field
B) Tractor
C) Crop
D) Farm
Q7.
Camera : Photograph :: Keyboard : ?
A) Computer
B) Typing
C) Mouse
D) Screen
Q8.
Tailor : Needle :: Painter : ?
A) Wall
B) Brush
C) Colour
D) Painting
Q9.
Milk : Butter :: Wheat : ?
A) Farm
B) Flour
C) Bread
D) Grain
Q10.
Bottle : Glass :: Shirt : ?
A) Cotton
B) Cloth
C) Tailor
D) Wear
Answers 1–10 bhejo. Iske baad main tumhe Word Analogy ke thode tricky questions dunga, jahan 2 options related honge aur tumhe exact relationship pakadna padega.
❌ Q5 ko microscopic way mein samjho
Fire : Smoke :: Rain : ?
Fire → Smoke
Yahan relationship hai:
Cause → Effect
•	Fire = cause 
•	Smoke = effect 
Ab Rain ka effect kya ho sakta hai?
Rain → Flood
इसलिए answer = C. Flood
Tumne Water choose kiya.
Problem ye hai ki:
Rain → Water bhi related hai, lekin ye Cause → Effect wala relationship nahi hai.
Rain water se related hai, lekin question mein relationship effect ka tha.
🔑 Golden Rule
Analogy mein:
Sirf relation hona enough nahi hai; same TYPE ka relation hona chahiye.
________________________________________
Ab next level: PART 2B — Tricky Word Analogy
Ab questions thode exam-oriented honge. Yahan options mein 2 related answers jaan-bujhkar ho sakte hain.

PART 2C — Word Analogy के Major Patterns
इसमें हम लगभग 15–20 अलग-अलग relationships cover करेंगे, जैसे:
•	Worker → Tool 
•	Worker → Product 
•	Person → Place 
•	Animal → Home 
•	Animal → Sound 
•	Material → Product 
•	Cause → Effect 
•	Object → Function 
•	Part → Whole 
•	Creator → Creation 
•	Male → Female 
•	Young One → Adult 
•	Country → Capital 
•	Country → Currency 
•	Instrument → Measurement
🧠 PART 2C — Important Word Relationships
1. Male → Female
King : Queen :: Man : Woman
Relationship:
Male → Female
Examples:
•	Bull → Cow 
•	Horse → Mare 
•	Lion → Lioness 
•	Actor → Actress 
•	Uncle → Aunt 
⚠️ Dhyan: har word ka grammatical gender nahi, actual male-female pair dekho.
________________________________________
2. Young One → Adult
Calf : Cow :: Foal : Horse
Calf = young cow
Foal = young horse
Relationship:
Young → Adult
Examples:
•	Puppy → Dog 
•	Kitten → Cat 
•	Cub → Lion 
•	Chick → Hen/Bird 
________________________________________
3. Creator → Creation
Author : Book :: Painter : Painting
Author creates Book.
Painter creates Painting.
Relationship:
Creator → Creation
Examples:
•	Poet → Poem 
•	Composer → Music 
•	Sculptor → Sculpture 
•	Director → Film 
________________________________________
4. Country → Capital
India : New Delhi :: France : Paris
Relationship:
Country → Capital
Examples:
•	Japan → Tokyo 
•	Nepal → Kathmandu 
•	Bangladesh → Dhaka 
•	Australia → Canberra 
________________________________________
5. Country → Currency
India : Rupee :: Japan : Yen
Relationship:
Country → Currency
Examples:
•	USA → Dollar 
•	UK → Pound 
•	Bangladesh → Taka 
•	China → Yuan 
________________________________________
6. Instrument → Measurement
Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : Pressure
Thermometer measures temperature.
Barometer measures atmospheric pressure.
Relationship:
Instrument → What it measures
Examples:
•	Speedometer → Speed 
•	Ammeter → Current 
•	Voltmeter → Voltage 
•	Odometer → Distance 
________________________________________
7. Part → Whole
Abhi tak humne Whole → Part dekha tha.
Example:
Finger : Hand :: Wheel : Car
Finger is a part of Hand.
Wheel is a part of Car.
Relationship:
Part → Whole
⚠️ Direction important hai:
Hand : Finger = Whole → Part
Finger : Hand = Part → Whole
________________________________________
8. Object → Material
Table : Wood :: Shirt : Cotton
Table is made of wood.
Shirt is made of cotton.
Relationship:
Object → Material
________________________________________
9. Material → Product
Iska reverse:
Wood : Furniture :: Cotton : Cloth
Relationship:
Material → Product
याद रखो:
Wood → Furniture
Material → Product
लेकिन
Furniture → Wood
Object → Material
Direction बदल गई तो answer भी बदल सकता है.
________________________________________
10. Cause → Effect
Exercise : Fitness :: Study : Knowledge
Exercise leads to fitness.
Study leads to knowledge.
Relationship:
Cause → Effect
________________________________________
🔥 अब एक बहुत important concept: Direction
Analogy में relationship की direction बहुत important है.
Example:
Doctor : Hospital
Person → Workplace
लेकिन:
Hospital : Doctor
Place → Person
दोनों related हैं, लेकिन relationship अलग है.
इसी तरह:
Wood : Furniture
Material → Product
Furniture : Wood
Product → Material
🎯 CET Trick
हर question में arrow लगाओ:
A → B
फिर वही arrow:
C → ?
बस direction उलटी मत करना.
________________________________________

🧠 3-Step Formula
Har question mein:
Step 1: A → B dekho
Step 2: Relationship bolo
Step 3: Same relationship C → ? par lagao

Seed → Plant = starting stage → developed form
Egg → Chicken

chapters.subject: Reasoning
chapters.title: Number Analogy
chapters.content:
NUMBER ANALOGY

इसमें हम बिल्कुल zero से शुरू करेंगे:

1.   Number Analogy क्या है?
2. Addition/Subtraction pattern
3. Multiplication/Division pattern
4. Square/Cube based analogy
5. Difference pattern
6. Mixed operations
7. Two-step/three-step patterns
8. CET-level tricky questions
9. Final Number Analogy test

🔢 PART 3A — Number Analogy का Basic Concept

Number Analogy का सामान्य format:

A : B :: C : ?

लेकिन यहाँ words के बजाय numbers के बीच mathematical relationship ढूँढना होता है।

Example 1

5 : 10 :: 7 : ?

देखो:

5 → 10

यहाँ:

5 × 2 = 10

तो वही relation:

7 × 2 = 14

✅ Answer = 14

Example 2

8 : 12 :: 10 : ?

8 → 12

8 + 4 = 12

तो:

10 + 4 = 14

✅ Answer = 14

Example 3

20 : 15 :: 12 : ?

20 → 15

20 − 5 = 15

तो:

12 − 5 = 7

✅ Answer = 7

🧠 सबसे पहला Rule

Number Analogy में हमेशा पहले:

A → B

का mathematical relation निकालो।

फिर वही operation:

C → ?

पर लगाओ।

🔥 सबसे Common Operations

शुरुआत में आपको मुख्यतः ये operations check करने हैं:

1. Addition

7 : 12

7 + 5 = 12

2. Subtraction

15 : 9

15 − 6 = 9

3. Multiplication

6 : 30

6 × 5 = 30

4. Division

40 : 8

40 ÷ 5 = 8

5. Square

5 : 25

5² = 25

6. Cube

3 : 27

3³ = 27

⚠️ लेकिन एक बहुत जरूरी बात

हर question में केवल + / − / × / ÷ देखकर answer मत निकालना।

Example:

5 : 25 :: 7 : ?

5 → 25

Possible:

5 × 5 = 25

लेकिन यह actually:

5² = 25

तो:

7² = 49

🧠 Number Analogy Solving Order

जब question देखो तो इस order में check करो:

① + / −

② × / ÷

③ Square / Cube

④ Combination

अभी हम पहले सिर्फ single-operation analogy करेंगे।

🔢 PART 3B — Mixed Number Analogy

अब difficulty एक level बढ़ाते हैं।

यहाँ relation थोड़ा छिपा होगा। आपको सिर्फ + − × ÷ नहीं, बल्कि 2-step operation पहचानना होगा।

Example:

5 : 13 :: 7 : ?

5 × 2 + 3 = 13

तो:

7 × 2 + 3 = 17

Example:

6 : 15 :: 8 : ?

6 × 2 + 3 = 15

8 × 2 + 3 = 19

Example:

10 : 21 :: 7 : ?

10 × 2 + 1 = 21

7 × 2 + 1 = 15

⚠️ लेकिन एक बात

हर question में relation unique होना चाहिए। अगर multiple simple patterns possible हों, तो हम ऐसा pattern चुनेंगे जो सभी numbers के साथ logically consistent हो और standard reasoning convention के अनुसार हो।

🔢 PART 3D — Tricky Number Analogy

1. n² + Constant

Example:

5 : 28 :: 7 : ?

Pehle 5 → 28 dekho:

  • 5² = 25
  • 25 + 3 = 28

To rule hai:

n² + 3

Ab 7 par:

  • 7² = 49
  • 49 + 3 = 52

✅ Answer = 52

2. n² − Constant

Example:

6 : 32 :: 8 : ?

  • 6² = 36
  • 36 − 4 = 32

Rule = n² − 4

Ab:

  • 8² = 64
  • 64 − 4 = 60

✅ Answer = 60

3. n³ + Constant

Example:

4 : 68 :: 5 : ?

  • 4³ = 64
  • 64 + 4 = 68

Yahan rule actually n³ + n hai.

Ab 5:

  • 5³ = 125
  • 125 + 5 = 130

✅ Answer = 130

4. n × (n + 1)

Ye important pattern hai.

Example:

5 : 30 :: 7 : ?

5 × (5+1)

= 5 × 6
= 30

Ab 7:

7 × 8 = 56

✅ Answer = 56

Dhyan do:

n × (n+1) = n²+n

Isliye ye wahi pattern hai jo hum pehle kar chuke hain.

5. n × (n − 1)

Example:

6 : 30 :: 8 : ?

6 × (6−1)

= 6 × 5
= 30

Ab:

8 × 7 = 56

✅ Answer = 56

Ye mathematically:

n² − n

ke equal hai.

6. Mixed Pattern

Kabhi question mein pattern simple +/− nahi hota.

Example:

4 : 19 :: 6 : ?

Check:

4 × 4 = 16
16 + 3 = 19

Rule:

n² + 3

Ab:

6² + 3
= 36 + 3
= 39

⚡ CET Pattern पहचानने की Trick

Jab A : B diya ho, is order mein check karo:

Step 1

+ ya −

Step 2

× ya ÷

Step 3

×2 + something / ×3 + something

Step 4

n²

Step 5

n³

Step 6

n² ± constant

Step 7

n³ ± constant

Step 8

n² ± n
ya
n³ ± n

Sabse important: pehla relation jo fit ho us par turant mat rukna. Dekho kya woh uniquely aur consistently fit hota hai.

🔢 PART 3E — Advanced Number Analogy

सबसे पहले एक जरूरी बात

Advanced analogy में हमेशा n², n³ ही नहीं होगा। कभी:

  • × और + साथ में
  • × और − साथ में
  • दो numbers का product
  • digits के साथ operation
  • difference/square का relation
  • अलग-अलग लेकिन consistent mathematical pattern

आ सकता है।

इसलिए हमारा तरीका होगा:

पहले simple pattern → फिर mixed pattern → फिर advanced pattern

🔹 Type 1: Multiplication + Addition

Example

7 : 17 :: 9 : ?

देखो:

7 × 2 = 14
14 + 3 = 17

Rule:

n × 2 + 3

अब 9:

9 × 2 = 18
18 + 3 = 21

✅ Answer = 21

🔹 Type 2: Multiplication − Addition

Example

8 : 21 :: 10 : ?

8 × 3 = 24
24 − 3 = 21

Rule:

n × 3 − 3

अब:

10 × 3 − 3
= 30 − 3
= 27

✅ Answer = 27

🔹 Type 3: Multiplication + Multiplication

Example

6 : 42 :: 8 : ?

6 × 7 = 42

यानी:

n × (n+1)

अब:

8 × 9 = 72

✅ Answer = 72

यह pattern हमने पहले भी देखा है।

🔹 Type 4: Product of Consecutive Numbers

Example

9 : 72 :: 11 : ?

9 × 8 = 72

यानी:

n × (n−1)

अब:

11 × 10 = 110

✅ Answer = 110

🔹 Type 5: Difference Based

अब थोड़ा ध्यान देना।

Example

8 : 56 :: 10 : ?

8 × 7 = 56

लेकिन इसे ऐसे भी देख सकते हैं:

8² − 8 = 64 − 8 = 56

इसलिए:

10² − 10
= 100 − 10
= 90

यहाँ हमें equivalent form पहचाननी है।

🔹 Type 6: Digit-Based Pattern

ये थोड़ा अलग है।

Example

24 : 8 :: 35 : ?

24 के digits:

2 × 4 = 8

अब:

3 × 5 = 15

✅ Answer = 15

यहाँ number को पूरा number मानकर calculation नहीं करनी; digits को अलग-अलग देखना है।

🔹 Type 7: Digit Addition

Example

36 : 9 :: 47 : ?

3 + 6 = 9

अब:

4 + 7 = 11

✅ Answer = 11

🔹 Type 8: Square of Digits / Digit Relationship

Example:

23 : 13 :: 14 : ?

2² + 3²
= 4 + 9
= 13

अब:

1² + 4²
= 1 + 16
= 17

✅ Answer = 17

🧠 Advanced Pattern पहचानने का Order

जब CET में difficult analogy मिले तो:

Level 1

+ − × ÷

Level 2

×2 + 3, ×3 − 2

Level 3

n², n³

Level 4

n² ± n, n³ ± n

Level 5

n × (n+1) / n × (n−1)

Level 6

Digits पर operation

जैसे:

24 → 2×4

36 → 3+6

23 → 2²+3²
